summary: Adds a /download endpoint that serves files from the upload directory by name, and switches the dev server to bind all interfaces with debug enabled.

findings.title: Path traversal in download endpoint
findings.problem: The handler joins the raw name query parameter onto the upload directory and serves the result. os.path.join accepts ../ segments and discards the base when name is absolute.
findings.consequence: Any caller can read any file the server process can open, such as /etc/passwd or application secrets.
findings.fix: Use safe_join from werkzeug, or resolve the path and verify it stays under UPLOAD_DIR, before calling send_file.

findings.title: Werkzeug debugger enabled on all interfaces
findings.problem: The app now runs with debug enabled, which exposes the interactive Werkzeug debugger on every exception. Combined with the all-interfaces bind, the debugger is reachable from the network.
findings.consequence: Anyone who can reach port 5000 can trigger an error page and run arbitrary Python on the host.
findings.fix: Remove debug=True from app.run and read the debug setting from an environment variable such as FLASK_DEBUG for local use only.

findings.title: Dev server bound to all interfaces
findings.problem: The host changed from loopback to 0.0.0.0, so the Flask development server accepts connections from any network interface. The previous binding limited it to the local machine.
findings.consequence: The unauthenticated download endpoint and the debugger become reachable by every host on the network.
findings.fix: Restore host="127.0.0.1" or read the bind address from an environment variable so only deployments that need it opt in.

findings.title: New download endpoint has no test
findings.problem: The change adds a download handler with a 404 branch and a file response. The repository contains no test files, so no test exercises either path.
findings.consequence: Regressions in the 404 handling or path validation will ship unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a test module that calls /download with a missing, valid, and traversal name. Assert the response for each case.
